To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we show that a simple learning algorithm can efficiently learn CNNs, and that this is provable, and that this holds under natural assumptions on the input distribution.

(1) CNNs are efficiently learnable, (2) the algorithm learns a linear classifier, (3) the algorithm uses data-dependent features, (4) the algorithm is semi-supervised, and (5) the algorithm is provably efficient under some natural assumptions.

\begin{enumerate*} \item CNNs with data-driven features can be learned in polynomial time, \item the algorithm is provably efficient in the low-dimensional manifold case, \item this efficiency cannot be improved, and \item the algorithm learns a CNN, which generalizes to the test set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can a linear algorithm provably learn a deep CNN? We provide the first affirmative answer to this question.
